_comment: Tier definitions and SLO budgets — the single source of truth.
Read by k6 (benchmark/k6/lib/config.js, via open()) and by the reporter
(benchmark/collect/summarize.ts, via fs). It lives in JSON rather than in the
k6 script because both need it: if the numbers were duplicated, a threshold
change would silently stop matching the verdict printed in summary.md.
maxVus is a guard rail, not a suggestion. The scenarios enforce it, so
exam-day cannot be run at cohort scale against the local image and
edge-validation cannot be pointed at anything but the dev site.

local.name: local
local._slo_comment: Generous, because a dev machine under Docker Desktop has a noisy floor. The signal for this tier is the delta computed by compare.ts, not these gates.

dev.name: dev
dev.purpose: edge, TLS, auth and S3 validation — never capacity
dev._slo_comment: Includes CDN, TLS and tunnel overhead, so the budget is wider by design. The interesting output is the delta against tier 3's origin-direct numbers.

ec2.name: ec2
ec2.purpose: capacity, breaking point, recovery, queue behaviour
ec2._slo_comment: The only tier whose absolute numbers mean anything, because it is the only one with production's CPU and EBS behaviour. Recalibrate after the first clone run — these are estimates, not measurements.
